ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $6.90 Ryde voucher to the rider for the unexempted detour mileage; no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The trace settles that one off-route segment exists on this RydeTAXI trip: 17:37–17:53, 7.60 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.70 km, adding 4.89 km [F4], against an optimal 15.5 km and an actual 20.9 km [F1]. RD-1 makes that segment unexempted unless RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5 excuses it, and none does. RD-4 is closed by the record: no traffic incident near the route in the trip window [F15], and the only traffic facts are speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on PIE and CTE [F13][F14], above the band 1–2 condition of RD-4(b) and, per RD-4(c), no basis for exemption.

The rider's own message asked for "a 7-Eleven on the way", without naming any store [F9], and the driver answered only "Sure" [F10]. That is a rider-requested stop, but RD-3(a) exempts only when the rider named the place; a stop the rider asked for without naming a place does not excuse the driver's choice of a far one, so the segment counts under RD-3(b) — the driver himself concedes the store was his own choice [F12]. For the same reason RD-5 gives no cover: the message is neither a general route authorisation ("whichever way is faster") nor an agreement to a named road; it is a request for a short stop whose scope does not include the route to a store the driver picked [F9][F10][F12]. A statement written after the trip is a claim, not rider consent (G11), so [F12] cannot exempt the segment either.

Because this is a metered RydeTAXI trip, the extra distance entered the fare [F8], and RD-2 refunds the unexempted segment's extra_km at this trip's per-km rate taken from the fare record: $29.53 ÷ 20.94 km = $1.4102/km [F5][F8]. 4.89 km × $1.4102/km = $6.8957, rounded to $6.90 [F4][F5][RD-2]. The remaining $0.82 of the $7.71 billed excess is corridor/map-matching mileage that RD-2 expressly does not refund. The metered waiting item $1.19 for 4.6 min [F6] follows the meter and is not refundable under RD-3(c), and the rider does not claim it.

No account flag attaches: RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days, and the driver's profile shows 1 upheld dispute with route = 0 and no-show = 1 [F18]; profile facts cannot ground the route finding in any event. The safety screen found no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation in the chat, the complaint or the driver's statement [F9][F10][F12], and the record is complete (all messages timestamped [F11]), so the record settles every element this ruling needs.

segment_findings.reason: The rider's only routing message, sent 17:33 before the 17:37 segment, asked for 'a 7-Eleven on the way' and named no place [F9]; the driver's 'Sure' accepted a stop, not a chosen store or road [F10]. RD-3(a) exempts only a stop where the rider named the place, and RD-3(b) withholds exemption for the driver's own choice of store; RD-5 consent here reaches at most a short stop, never the route to a store the driver alone picked, and a post-trip statement is a claim, not consent (G11) [F12]. The segment's 4.89 km extra_km therefore counts and is refundable under RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: Quantum partly rejected: the $6.90 is right for the segment's 4.89 km [F4] at $1.4102/km ($29.53 ÷ 20.94 km) [F5][F8], but the claim is measured against the whole 4.89 km of the segment; the remainder of the billed excess ($7.71 − $6.8957 ≈ $0.82) is corridor/map-matching mileage RD-2 withholds.
Rejected: RD-6 requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1, and [F18] records 1 upheld dispute that is a no-show (route 0, no-show 1), and profile facts cannot decide the route finding; no flag_account.

Correct as far as it goes and accepted — the $1.19 metered waiting charge [F6] follows the meter on a RydeTAXI trip under RD-3(c) and is not refunded; it is cited as background, not as a recoverable item.
Rejected as to the ceiling: the billed excess of $7.71 [F5] is the ceiling on the dispute, not the entitlement — RD-2 refunds only the unexempted segment's 4.89 km extra_km [F4][F5].

Accepted only in part: profile facts cannot decide the route finding under RD-6, and [F18] shows no prior upheld route dispute, so no account referral — but that does not reduce the refund the GPS segment supports.
